Docs/Layouts

Layouts

A layout is a layout.ts or layout.tsx file that wraps every page at or below its directory. Use one when several pages share the same shell, navigation, sidebar, or metadata.

Defining a layout

The default export receives child, a function that renders the page or the next layout down. Call it where the inner content should go.

ts
// pages/layout.ts
export default function Layout({ child }: { child: () => Element }) {
    return div({ class: "shell" },
        header({ class: "site-header" },
            h1("My Site"),
        ),
        main({ class: "site-main" }, child()),
    );
}

This is the root layout, so it wraps every page in the project.

A layout deeper in the tree only wraps its own directory:

ts
// pages/dashboard/layout.ts
export default function Layout({ child }: { child: () => Element }) {
    return div({ class: "dashboard" },
        Sidebar(),
        section({ class: "dashboard-content" }, child()),
    );
}

pages/dashboard/page.ts and pages/dashboard/settings/page.ts both get this layout. Pages outside pages/dashboard/ do not.

If you prefer TSX, the same layout might look like this:

tsx
// pages/layout.tsx
export default function Layout({ child }: { child: () => Element }) {
    return <div class="shell">
        <header class="site-header">
            <h1>My Site</h1>
        </header>
        <main class="site-main">{child()}</main>
    </div>;
}

Nesting

Layouts nest from the outside in. With this tree:

text
pages/
  layout.ts
  dashboard/
    layout.ts
    page.ts
    settings/
      page.ts

/dashboard renders the root layout, then the dashboard layout, then the page.

/dashboard/settings renders the root layout, then the dashboard layout, then the settings page.

The root layout's child() renders the dashboard layout. The dashboard layout's child() renders the page. That's why child is a function. Each layout decides when the inner tree runs.

Passing data down

child accepts props, which are passed to the next layout or page.

ts
// pages/dashboard/layout.ts
export default async function Layout({ child }: {
    child: (props: { user: User }) => Element;
}) {
    const user = await getCurrentUser();

    return div({ class: "dashboard" },
        Sidebar({ user }),
        main(child({ user })),
    );
}
ts
// pages/dashboard/page.ts
export default function Page({ user }: { user: User }) {
    return h1(`Welcome back, ${user.name}`);
}

The page still gets its route params. If the route has an [id] segment, the page can accept both user and id.

Async layouts

Layouts can be async. They run on the server, either at build time for static pages or per request for dynamic ones, so you can fetch data, read from a database, or use server-only modules directly.

ts
// pages/blog/layout.ts
export default async function Layout({ child }: {
    child: () => Promise<Element>;
}) {
    const categories = await db.categories.findAll();

    return div({ class: "blog" },
        CategoryNav({ categories }),
        article({ class: "blog-content" }, await child()),
    );
}

The layout function itself never ships to the browser. Components rendered inside it hydrate normally.

Metadata

Export metadata from a layout. It can be an array or a function, and it can be async.

ts
// pages/layout.ts
export const metadata = () => [
    link({ rel: "icon", href: "/favicon.svg" }),
    meta({ name: "theme-color", content: "#080808" }),
];
ts
// pages/about/page.ts
export const metadata = () => [
    title("About"),
    meta({ name: "description", content: "About this site." }),
];

A layout's metadata function receives the route params:

ts
// pages/blog/layout.ts
export const metadata = ({ slug }: { slug: string }) => [
    meta({ property: "og:type", content: "article" }),
];

Metadata from layouts and the page is merged into <head>, with layout metadata first. Keep global tags in the root layout and page-specific tags in the page. If you set <title> in both places, you'll get two title tags.

Styles

CSS imported from a layout applies to every page under it. It's linked before the page's own CSS, so page styles can override layout styles.

ts
// pages/dashboard/layout.ts
import "./dashboard.css";

Dynamic layouts

Export isDynamic = true from a layout to make every page under it render per request.

ts
// pages/admin/layout.ts
export const isDynamic = true;

This is useful when a whole section needs runtime rendering. Avoid doing it in the root layout, because that turns every page in the project dynamic. See Dynamic Pages for more.

Notes

  • child is a function, not a node. Call it where the inner content should render.
  • Layouts apply to pages, not API routes.
  • A layout can live in a directory with no page of its own, as long as there are pages below it.
  • Both layout.ts and layout.tsx are supported.
  • A layout does not have a URL of its own. It only runs as part of a page.
